source.title: Impact of empagliflozin added on to basal insulin in type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on basal insulin: a 78-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluated the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of empagliflozin 10 mg and 25 mg once daily versus placebo for 78 weeks as add-on therapy to basal insulin in patients with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes.
This was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase IIb trial conducted from November 2009 to May 2012 at 97 centers in seven countries.
Randomization used a third-party interactive voice and web response system in a 1:1:1 ratio and was stratified by screening HbA1c below versus at least 8.5% and by center.
The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT01011868 and all patients provided written informed consent.
Adults had type 2 diabetes with screening HbA1c greater than 7% and no more than 10%.

population.label: Adults with type 2 diabetes and screening HbA1c >7% to <=10%

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible patients had body mass index no more than 45 kg/m2.

population.label: Adults with type 2 diabetes on basal insulin

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible basal insulin therapy was glargine or detemir at least 20 IU/day or NPH insulin at least 14 IU/day, with the dose stable within 10% for at least 12 weeks before randomization.

population.label: Adults on stable basal insulin
inclusion_criteria: Glargine or detemir >=20 IU/day or NPH >=14 IU/day
Basal insulin dose unchanged by >10% for >=12 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Metformin and sulfonylurea were permitted background therapies if unchanged for at least 12 weeks before randomization.

population.label: Adults on basal insulin with optional oral background therapy
inclusion_criteria: Metformin and/or sulfonylurea permitted if unchanged for >=12 weeks

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 were excluded.

atoms.canonical_statement: Recent myocardial infarction, stroke, or transient ischemic attack within 3 months before consent was an exclusion criterion.

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients with frequent hypoglycemic events on basal insulin therapy, in the investigator opinion, were excluded.

atoms.canonical_statement: Use of chronic short-acting insulin or a GLP-1 receptor agonist within 3 months before consent was excluded.

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary endpoint used ANCOVA with treatment and region as fixed effects and baseline HbA1c as a linear covariate.
Values after rescue therapy were set to missing and imputed using last observation carried forward for the main ANCOVA efficacy analyses.

The supplement specified separate dose-wise hierarchical testing at two-sided alpha 0.025 for week-18 HbA1c superiority, week-78 insulin-dose superiority, week-78 HbA1c noninferiority, and then week-78 HbA1c superiority.
A planned sample size of 150 patients per group provided 88% power to detect a 0.4 percentage-point HbA1c treatment difference assuming a common standard deviation of 1.0% at alpha 0.025.
Sensitivity analyses used mixed-model repeated measures on observed cases, while categorical HbA1c target analyses used logistic regression with noncompleters considered failures.
A total of 494 patients were randomized: 170 to placebo, 169 to empagliflozin 10 mg, and 155 to empagliflozin 25 mg.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that empagliflozin added to basal insulin for 78 weeks improved glycemic control and reduced body weight with a similar risk of hypoglycemia to placebo.

The discussion states that empagliflozin 10 mg and 25 mg improved glycemic control and reduced insulin requirements and weight over 78 weeks, while genitourinary infections occurred more often with empagliflozin.
Because basal insulin was not optimized with a forced treat-to-target algorithm, the full effect of empagliflozin on glycemic control and insulin dose could not be established.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Insulin dose was not optimized with a forced treat-to-target algorithm.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study did not control changes in antihypertensive medication, which could have influenced observed blood pressure changes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Changes in antihypertensive medication were not controlled.

atoms.canonical_statement: Only 73% of randomized patients completed 78 weeks of treatment, creating attrition that matters for long-term interpretation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only 360 of 494 randomized patients completed 78 weeks.

atoms.canonical_statement: The principal week-18 efficacy analysis used a completer population with LOCF after rescue-therapy censoring, which makes the primary estimate dependent on missing-data assumptions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Primary efficacy analysis used week-18 completers and LOCF after rescue-therapy censoring.
